title: A proper birational morphism of integral curves is finite
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $C$ and $E$ be integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] separated schemes of finite type over $k$, each of dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $p:E\to C$ be a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] dominant $k$-morphism inducing an isomorphism $k(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}k(E)$ of function fields [def-sc-function-field]. Then $p$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0AB7 (lemma-finite-in-codim-1), especially the hypotheses and proof: for each point of the one-dimensional target, properness and the finite generic field extension give finiteness over a neighbourhood; finiteness is local on the target.
